memos.headline: S08 at 52-week high with clean trend; S05 parabolic and overextended; S01 and S10 breaking down
memos.body: I see the strongest technical setups in S08 and S07, both sitting near 52-week highs with powerful 12w and 26w momentum and positive relative strength versus SPY. S08 closed at 278.85, literally at its 52-week high with RSI 68.3—strong but not yet overbought—and +22.7% above its 200d mean, which I view as a healthy uptrend rather than overextension given the 2.07% ATR. S05 is the most dangerous name on the board: +19.5% above its 50d mean, +58.5% above its 200d mean, RSI 73.5, and a 90% 26-week return—this is a parabolic move that historically mean-reverts hard. On the weak side, S01 is in a clear downtrend at -6.9% below its 200d mean with negative 12w and 26w returns and -12.2% relative strength vs SPY over 12 weeks, while S10 has broken down sharply with a -14.5% drawdown and -13.3% 4-week relative strength. I would fade the extremes and ride the clean trends.

views.note: At 52-week high, RSI 68 not yet overbought, strong relative strength; would reassess on a close below the 50d mean (~262).
Near highs with +37% 12w return and +31.7% 12w relative strength, RSI 62.9 still has room; risk is the 4w relative weakness, would cut below 530.
Parabolic extension at +58.5% above 200d mean with RSI 73.5 screams mean-reversion risk; would flip long only on a pullback to the 50d area (~268).
Persistent downtrend: -6.9% below 200d mean, -17.6% drawdown, negative relative strength across all timeframes; would reconsider above 159 (200d mean area).
Sharp breakdown with -14.5% drawdown, RSI 41.5, and worst 4w relative strength in the universe at -13.3%; needs to reclaim 187 (50d area) to stabilize.
Quiet uptrend near highs with only -2.3% drawdown, RSI 58 mid-range, and low ATR 2.31%—a steady compounder; would exit below 300.
Below 50d mean with -6.9% 4w relative strength but RSI 45 approaching oversold; watching for a bounce above 510 to turn constructive.
Massive -46% drawdown from highs and trading 10% below 200d mean signals structural damage, but the +5.9% weekly bounce hints at a possible base; need a close above 345 to get interested.

memos.headline: S10 and S05 Show Durable Earnings Power; S02 and S09 Flash Cash-Flow Compression Warnings
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe between names with expanding margins and accelerating earnings versus those suffering margin erosion despite top-line growth. S10 stands out with 62.5% YoY revenue growth, a 56.0% net margin, and only $8.47B in total debt — the cleanest earnings profile in the group. S05 delivers 34.2% net margins on $102.35B of revenue with net income up 33.0% YoY, and its $14.79B debt load is modest relative to earnings power. On the other end, S02 posted a 61.2% YoY decline in net income to just $2.35B on $113.16B of revenue (2.1% net margin) while carrying $80.14B in debt — a classic cash-flow compression setup I refuse to pay for. S09 is also deteriorating with revenue down 5.2% YoY, net income down 12.3%, and an 8.8% net margin on $32.82B of debt; I need to see a revenue inflection before getting constructive.

views.note: 62.5% revenue growth, 56.0% net margin, minimal leverage at $8.47B debt — the strongest earnings momentum and balance sheet in the universe.
34.2% net margin with 33.0% YoY net income growth and low $14.79B debt make this a high-quality compounder; would reassess if margins dip below 30%.
18.4% revenue growth and 35.7% net margin are strong, though 12.5% net income growth lags revenue growth, suggesting some margin pressure worth monitoring.
Revenue of $180.17B growing 13.4% YoY is impressive at scale, but 11.8% net margin and $55.10B debt keep me neutral until I see margin expansion sustain.
Net income surged 86.4% YoY to $27.47B but $90.68B in total debt and only 7.9% revenue growth suggest the earnings jump may not be durable without top-line acceleration.
31.0% net margin is healthy but $427.20B in total debt dwarfs the rest of the universe; earnings durability hinges on credit cycle dynamics I cannot fully assess from this filing alone.
21.2% net margin and 20% net income growth are solid, but only 3.0% revenue growth on $22.39B suggests limited top-line momentum; need to see revenue re-accelerate.
Revenue grew 9.5% YoY but net income fell 6.7% with a 13.0% margin and $31.74B debt — margin compression is a yellow flag, though not yet severe enough to avoid.
Revenue declining 5.2% YoY with net income down 12.3% and an 8.8% net margin on $32.82B debt signals deteriorating earnings power; would reconsider on a revenue inflection.
Net income collapsed 61.2% YoY to $2.35B on a razor-thin 2.1% margin while carrying $80.14B in debt — textbook cash-flow compression I will not own.

memos.headline: Fed in Easing Mode but Sticky 3% CPI and Rising Unemployment Signal a Cautious Slowdown Regime
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in an easing cycle — the upper bound has dropped 75bp over the past year to 4.00%, with 50bp of that in the last three months alone. However, headline CPI is running at 3.0% YoY, which remains above target and limits the pace of further cuts. Unemployment has risen 30bp over three months to 4.4%, confirming a softening labor market that justifies the easing bias but also flags cyclical risk. The 10y yield at 4.02% has declined 20bp over three months, and the 10y-2y spread at +0.55pp has re-steepened sharply (+46bp YoY), which is consistent with a late-cycle normalization rather than imminent recession. A CPI print accelerating above 3.5% or unemployment jumping above 4.7% would force me to revisit this 'gradual easing into mild slowdown' call.

views.note: Duration-sensitive growth benefits from falling front-end rates and declining 10y yields in an easing cycle with a steepening curve.
Banks gain from a positively sloped curve (+55bp 10y-2y) but face headwinds from slowing loan demand as unemployment rises and rate cuts compress NIM on the short end.
Staples offer defensive positioning as unemployment trends higher and the labor market softens, while their dividend yields become more attractive relative to falling Treasury yields.
Cyclicals face the most direct risk from rising unemployment and a slowing economy, and sticky inflation limits the fiscal/monetary support that could cushion demand.
Energy is caught between softening demand from the slowdown and potential supply-side support; macro signals are mixed so I lack conviction either way.
With the Fed easing and 10y yields declining, long-duration growth sectors should see multiple expansion; the 3% CPI is the key risk to monitor.

memos.headline: Earnings-Driven Sentiment Divergence: S07 and S03 Stand Out Positively While S10, S04, and S06 Flash Negative Signals
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in post-earnings sentiment across the universe. S07 posted an extraordinary +11.6% reaction to its 10/29 results and S03 surged +9.6% on its 10/30 print—both signaling strong positive narrative shifts that may still have momentum, especially with S03 filing a follow-up Other Events 8-K on 11/20 suggesting continued corporate activity. On the negative side, S10's most recent earnings on 11/19 drew a -3.2% reaction, S04 dropped -2.9% on its 10/29 results, and S06 fell -1.9% on its 10/14 report—these names carry deteriorating tone that I don't think is fully priced yet given the recency of S10's miss. S08, S01, S02, and S09 all had muted earnings reactions (ranging from -0.4% to +0.5%), leaving me neutral on those names absent a clearer directional catalyst.

views.note: The +11.6% earnings reaction is the strongest in the universe and suggests a genuine positive narrative shift that could sustain.
A +9.6% earnings pop plus a follow-up Other Events filing on 11/20 point to ongoing positive momentum and corporate activity.
The -3.2% reaction to the most recent (11/19) earnings is fresh and suggests negative sentiment has not yet been fully absorbed.
A -2.9% post-earnings drop on 10/29 reflects disappointed expectations; no subsequent positive catalysts have emerged.
Earnings reaction of -1.9% on 10/14 and subsequent filings show no tone improvement; negative drift may persist.
A flat +0.2% earnings reaction and high filing volume (six 8-Ks) suggest noise rather than a clear directional narrative.
Muted +0.5% earnings reaction and governance-related filings (bylaws, officer changes) are not sentiment-moving events.
Near-flat -0.3% earnings reaction and a string of non-financial filings leave no clear sentiment direction.
A solid +2.5% earnings reaction and a follow-up Other Events filing suggest modestly positive tone, though the move is less decisive than S07 or S03.
A -0.4% earnings reaction is essentially flat—no sentiment signal to act on.

memos.headline: Rising Policy Uncertainty and Softening Oil Signal Geopolitical Headwinds, but No Clear Structural Shift Yet
memos.body: I see a mixed but cautiously negative geopolitical backdrop as of today. The Economic Policy Uncertainty Index sits at 334.67, down 13.3% over the past month but still up 24.2% over three months, suggesting that while acute policy anxiety has eased somewhat, the structural level of uncertainty remains elevated relative to the summer. WTI crude at $58.81/bbl, down 7.5% over three months, points to weakening global demand expectations or easing supply fears—neither consistent with an imminent energy-security crisis but potentially reflecting demand destruction from trade-policy friction. HY OAS has widened 22 bps over three months to 3.00%, and VIX is up ~16% over the same window to 17.21, both consistent with markets pricing incrementally higher policy risk. Without specific GDELT event data on sanctions escalation or export-control actions, I lack conviction on any single structural geopolitical catalyst and am treating the current environment as a moderately elevated risk regime where names with heavy cross-border or energy exposure deserve caution.

views.note: Four 8-K filings in six weeks suggest active corporate developments, but without content detail I cannot assess geopolitical exposure; staying neutral pending clarity.
Four filings since early October indicate material corporate activity; elevated policy uncertainty warrants monitoring but no directional call without more detail.
Two 8-Ks in October and widening HY spreads suggest caution, but no specific geopolitical trigger identified to take a directional stance.
Single 8-K on Nov 20 with no content detail; elevated 3m policy uncertainty keeps me sidelined.
With WTI down 7.5% over three months and policy uncertainty still elevated on a 3m basis, I lean cautious on names that may carry energy or trade-sensitive exposure until the macro picture clarifies.
Single Reg FD filing in late October; no geopolitical signal strong enough to differentiate from the broader cautious backdrop.

We avoid parabolic extensions (S05), structural breakdowns (S01, S10, S02), and deteriorating earnings (S09).
